tesi: round duration falls as expected agency costs rise; ventures that go public get more rounds.

tesi: staging with convertible securities keeps the option to stop.
estrazione: The paper states that stage financing gives the venture capitalist the option to abandon the venture when the project's forward-looking value is negative. Its model shows that this option induces the entrepreneur to engage in window dressing, biasing the interim signal to reduce the probability of liquidation. Convertible securities are shown to deter this behaviour, because window dressing also raises the probability that the VC converts. The contribution is that convertibles dominate debt-plus-equity within staging, not that convertibles are what keeps the option to stop.
citazione: The venture capitalist retains the option to abandon the venture whenever the forward looking net present value of the project is negative.
frase_paper: Cornelli and Yosha (2003) model stage financing as giving the venture capitalist the option to abandon the project, and show that convertible securities reduce the entrepreneur's incentive to window-dress interim performance to avoid liquidation.

limiti_vs_noi: Pure theory with no data; it concerns contract design (convertible debt or warrants) and not the timing of rounds, the gap between rounds or exit outcomes.
note: The tesi as worded attributes the option to stop to 'staging with convertible securities'. In the txt the option comes from staging itself (introduction); convertibles protect the quality of the signal on which the stop decision rests. tesi: entrepreneurship as experimentation; cheaper experimentation changes how VC funds early bets.
estrazione: The paper argues that entrepreneurship is fundamentally about experimentation because the knowledge needed to succeed cannot be known in advance. It also argues that technological change has sharply lowered the cost of running experiments, especially in software and internet firms. This widens the funding sources beyond traditional VCs and lets startups that would not have been funded before (for example young, first-time founders) receive financing. Staged VC financing is described as the way investors respond to this uncertainty.
citazione: The lower costs associated with initial experiments implies that those with pools of capital smaller than typical venture capitalists can more easily become involved in these financing decisions.
posizione: Frictions for the Process of Experimentation: Costs of Experiments

limiti_vs_noi: Conceptual essay with anecdotes, no estimation; the cost decline is described mainly for software and internet firms; the figure is attributed to industry observers, not measured; it does not study the time between rounds or exit.

tesi: the signalling value of patents is strong at round 1 and largely gone by round 2.

tesi: VC investment responds to public-market signals; experienced VCs expand most in hot markets without lower success.
estrazione: The paper finds that VC firms with the most industry experience raise their investments most when public market signals (industry Q) improve, more than less experienced firms. Success rates are slightly lower in hot markets overall, but the difference is small and not statistically significant, and experienced firms show much less decline (2% vs 11% for low-experience firms). At industry level, investment responds to Q but shows no significant pattern with IPO activity, so 'responds to public-market signals' holds for Q, not for both signals. 'Without lower success' is stronger than 'no real degradation' / 'not adversely to a significant extent'.
citazione: increase their investments during market booms with no real degradation in their performance
frase_paper: Gompers et al. (2008) find that VC firms with the most industry experience increase their investments most when public market signals (industry Q) improve, with no significant degradation in success, in US VC deals from 1975 to 1998.
frase_slide: Industry-experienced VCs invest most when public markets heat up, with no real drop in success (Gompers et al., 2008)

tesi: abundant capital lowers investors' bargaining power and raises start-up values.
estrazione: In the model, more capital market competition (more venture capitalists relative to entrepreneurs) raises the entrepreneur's outside option and shifts bargaining in favour of the entrepreneur, lowering the VC's equity share. Pre-money and post-money valuations are therefore increasing in competition (Proposition 2). The total value created in the start-up is first increasing and then decreasing in competition, so 'start-up values' in general do not rise monotonically. The result is a theoretical prediction, not an empirical finding.
citazione: Both the pre-money valuation and the post-money valuation are increasing in the level of capital market competition
frase_paper: Inderst and Mueller (2004) model that greater capital market competition shifts bargaining power towards entrepreneurs, lowers the VC's equity share and raises pre- and post-money valuations.
frase_slide: In theory, more competition for deals shifts bargaining to entrepreneurs and raises valuations (Inderst & Mueller, 2004)
dati_metodo: Equilibrium model of contracting, Nash bargaining and search between entrepreneurs and venture capitalists; short- and long-run comparative statics in capital market competition; no own data.
limiti_vs_noi: Theory without data; the prediction concerns valuations (pre- and post-money), not total start-up value, which is non-monotonic in competition. Not about exit or round timing.
note: Tesi says 'raises start-up values': the txt supports valuations (Prop. 2), while total value created is first increasing then decreasing in competition. 'Abundant capital' is modelled as the ratio of VCs to entrepreneurs; the first part (lower investor bargaining power) is supported. Wording must shrink to valuations.

tesi: closer VC monitoring raises innovation and IPO rates.
estrazione: The paper uses new airline routes that cut travel time between VCs and their existing portfolio companies as an exogenous reduction in monitoring costs. In a difference-in-differences design, treatment raises patent counts (3.1%), citations per patent (5.8%), the probability of IPO (1.0%) and of a successful exit via IPO or acquisition (1.4%). The authors interpret this as VC involvement increasing innovation and exit success.
citazione: the treatment increases the probability of going public by 1.0% and the probability of having a successful exit (via IPO or acquisition) by 1.4%
frase_paper: Bernstein et al. (2016) find that exogenous reductions in VC travel time to portfolio companies, which proxy for closer monitoring, raise patenting and citations per patent and the probability of an IPO or successful exit, in US VC-backed companies.
frase_slide: Closer VC monitoring raises innovation and IPO/exit probability (Bernstein et al., 2016)
dati_metodo: US VC-portfolio company pairs (22,986 companies), patents to 2006; difference-in-differences on new airline routes cutting VC travel time, plus a survey of 306 VCs
numero_chiave: +1.0% probability of going public, +1.4% probability of a successful exit (IPO or acquisition), after a new direct flight route
limiti_vs_noi: Monitoring is proxied by travel-time cuts from new airline routes, not by round timing; sample is VC-portfolio company pairs with patent data to 2006, not 2012-2019; outcomes are yearly indicators, not exit within five years.
note: Causal wording is supported by the paper's quasi-experimental design; the source does not study the gap between rounds. Innovation measured by patents and citations.

tesi: CVC-backed firms are more innovative.
estrazione: The paper finds that CVC-backed entrepreneurial firms are more innovative than IVC-backed ones, measured by patenting outcomes (quantity and citations per patent), even though they are younger, riskier and less profitable. The result holds in a propensity score matching analysis of IPO firms and in a difference-in-differences analysis of the universe of VC-backed firms. The evidence is empirical, but the authors flag possible selection and treat it as association-type evidence on patenting.
citazione: We find that CVC-backed firms are more innovative, as measured by their patenting outcome, although they are younger, riskier, and less profitable than IVC-backed firms.
frase_paper: Chemmanur et al. (2014) find that CVC-backed firms are more innovative, as measured by patenting, than IVC-backed firms, in a sample of US VC-backed firms.
frase_slide: CVC-backed firms patent more than independent-VC-backed firms (Chemmanur et al., 2014)
dati_metodo: US VC-backed entrepreneurial firms (IPO firms for the baseline, plus the universe of VC-backed firms in a difference-in-differences), patent counts and citations 1976-2006 patent data; regressions, propensity score matching and diff-in-diff, CVC vs independent VC.
limiti_vs_noi: Innovation measured by patents, baseline on IPO firms only (survivors); period up to 2006, not 2012-2019; compares CVC vs IVC, not round timing or exit.
note: Innovativeness is patent-based; the tesi should keep that qualifier if used in the paper.

tesi: CVC invests to source external innovation.
estrazione: The paper finds that CVC entry concentrates in firms whose internal innovation has deteriorated, and that CVCs invest in startups with similar technological focus but non-overlapping knowledge base, then integrate those technologies (parent firms cite the startups' patents after investing). It concludes that the strategic motive is to fix innovation weaknesses after adverse shocks, and it rejects the alternative 'build on strengths' view. The tesi is broadly in line but omits the condition (deteriorating internal innovation) and the evidence is on parent-firm innovation, not on startup outcomes.
citazione: CVCs are used by firms experiencing deteriorating internal innovation to expose themselves to new technologies and regain their innovation edge.
frase_paper: Ma (2020) finds that corporate venture capital divisions are created mainly by firms whose internal innovation has deteriorated, and that they use investments in startups to access new technologies and recover their innovation edge.
frase_slide: CVCs are set up when internal innovation weakens, to access startup technologies (Ma, 2020)
dati_metodo: US public non-financial firms with CVC divisions (SDC VentureXpert/Compustat), CVC entry, investment and termination decisions; panel regressions with an instrument for internal innovation (technological obsolescence); patent-based innovation measures
limiti_vs_noi: Studies CVC parent firms (entry, investment, termination), not startup exit or round timing; sample of US public parents over a long period, not 2012-2019 first-round startups.
note: Narrower than the tesi: the motive is conditional on a decline in the parent's internal innovation, not a general motive.

tesi: angel-group funding improves survival and growth (regression discontinuity).
estrazione: In the regression discontinuity, ventures just above the funding threshold are more likely to be alive in Dec 2010 (Table 6a: 0.222, s.e. 0.081; 0.247, s.e. 0.095 with fixed effects, N = 130) and show better employment, patenting and Web traffic growth. Exit (IPO or acquisition) is only qualitatively higher and not statistically significant. The funding discontinuity is fuzzy (about a 32 percentage point jump in funding probability), so the authors use the border design only to confirm the qualitative direction; the tesi's causal verb 'improves' and the general word 'growth' go beyond this.
citazione: Ventures just above the threshold are more likely to survive, and they have superior operations in terms of employee counts, patenting, and Web traffic growth.
frase_paper: Kerr et al. (2014) find, using a regression discontinuity around the interest threshold of two US angel groups, that ventures just above the funding threshold are more likely to survive and show better employment, patenting and Web traffic growth, while the higher exit rate is not statistically significant.

tesi: industries differ permanently in exit rates and specialisation.
estrazione: The txt studies how the specialisation of VC firms and individual VCs relates to the success of their investments, within and across industries. It takes industry success rates as varying by industry and year (used to build the Mix and Industry Alpha measures) and controls for industry and year fixed effects. in logit and probit the interaction effect is not the interaction coefficient.
estrazione: In nonlinear models the interaction effect is the cross derivative (or cross difference) of the expected outcome, not the coefficient on the interaction term or its marginal effect. It can be nonzero when the interaction coefficient is zero, it depends on the covariates, it can have different signs across observations, so the sign and t-test of the interaction coefficient do not give it. The formulas are stated to apply to logit and probit; the worked example is a logit.
citazione: The key point of this paper is that the interaction effect is found by computing cross derivatives (or differences), not by just looking at the coefficient on the interaction term.
frase_paper: Ai and Norton (2003) show that in logit and probit models the interaction effect is the cross derivative of the predicted probability, not the coefficient on the interaction term, and that its sign and significance can differ from those of that coefficient.
frase_slide: In logit, the interaction effect is not the interaction coefficient (Ai & Norton, 2003)
dati_metodo: Econometric derivation for nonlinear models (probit, logit, general F(x,b)); delta-method standard errors; illustrated with a logit of HMO enrolment on survey data.
numero_chiave: 72 articles (1980-1999, 13 economics journals) used interaction terms in nonlinear models; none interpreted the coefficient correctly
limiti_vs_noi: Methods paper; derives the correct interaction effect and its standard errors for a single interaction, with no startup or VC data. Our model has two interactions (two_rounds x heat, log_gap_r2 x heat), which the paper covers only as 'analogous'.
note: Derivation is shown for probit; logit is covered by the general formulas and the logit example. Tesi is not compound and not causal.

tesi: best practice is to estimate and show nonlinear interactions with marginal effects.
estrazione: Mize advises that, for nonlinear models such as logit, the size and significance of interaction effects be judged with marginal effects and tests of second differences, plotting predictions, and ignoring the product-term coefficient. Absent specific values of interest, average marginal effects summarise whether an interaction is present on average. This matches the tesi that nonlinear interactions are best estimated and shown with marginal effects.
citazione: Determine the size and significance of the effects of interest using marginal effects, not regression coefficients.
frase_paper: Mize (2019) recommends that, in nonlinear models such as logit, interaction effects be assessed and presented through marginal effects and tests of second differences rather than through the product-term coefficient.
frase_slide: In logit models, judge interactions with marginal effects, not the product-term coefficient (Mize, 2019)
dati_metodo: Methodological synthesis with worked examples (GSS-type survey data) on nonlinear interaction effects in linear and binary logit/probit models; recommends marginal effects and second differences.
numero_chiave: 50 of 53 ASR articles (2004-2016) on nonlinear interactions relied only on the product-term coefficient
limiti_vs_noi: Sociology-oriented guidance with survey examples; not specific to startup/VC data or to exit outcomes. It is a methods recommendation, not a finding about our data.
note: Tesi is a methods recommendation; the txt states it explicitly as best practice (also: plot predictions, second differences, average marginal effects).

tesi: with few clusters, cluster-robust p-values are too small; the wild cluster bootstrap fixes this.
estrazione: The txt says that Wald tests based on cluster-robust standard errors over-reject when the number of clusters is small (five to thirty), because the standard errors are biased downwards; in simulations a nominal 5% test rejects about 10% or more of the time. The wild cluster bootstrap-t brings rejection rates close to 0.05 in these linear-model simulations, but the txt also notes that bootstrap results depend on the resampling method and on discreteness, and the wild cluster bootstrap-se (not -t) under-rejects for G <= 10. The txt speaks of over-rejection of tests, not of p-values directly, and its evidence is for linear models.
citazione: asymptotic tests can over-reject, however, with few (five to thirty)
frase_paper: Cameron et al. (2008) show, in Monte Carlo simulations of linear models, that Wald tests based on cluster-robust standard errors over-reject with few clusters (five to thirty), and that a wild cluster bootstrap-t brings rejection rates close to the nominal 5%.
frase_slide: With few clusters, cluster-robust tests over-reject; wild cluster bootstrap-t restores nominal size in simulations (Cameron et al., 2008)
dati_metodo: Monte Carlo simulations of linear (OLS) models with clustered errors, G = 5 to 30 clusters, plus a Bertrand-Duflo-Mullainathan difference-in-differences replication and one empirical DID example; compares cluster-robust Wald tests with several cluster bootstrap-t methods
numero_chiave: Rejection rates of 10% with standard methods can be reduced to the nominal size of 5% (abstract); few clusters = five to thirty
limiti_vs_noi: Simulations and applications are linear OLS models (mostly difference-in-differences), not logit; G between 5 and 30, while our main exit models have 41 clusters (sector x year).
note: Tesi compound: (a) p-values too small = implied by over-rejection, not stated in terms of p-values; (b) 'fixes' is stronger than the txt: the wild cluster bootstrap-t brings size close to 0.05, with caveats. Narrower wording proposed.

tesi: round length chosen by the investor according to risk and monitoring costs.
estrazione: The txt argues that VCs weigh potential agency and monitoring costs when deciding how often to re-evaluate a project and supply capital, so duration should fall with expected agency costs. Empirically it supports the agency-cost side through industry proxies. Monitoring costs are not measured, and venture risk is not a variable; the paper leaves the importance of monitoring costs to future work.
citazione: Venture capitalists weigh potential agency and monitoring costs when determining how frequently they should reevaluate projects and supply capital.
frase_paper: Gompers (1995) argues that venture capitalists set how often they re-evaluate and refinance a project by weighing expected agency and monitoring costs, and finds shorter rounds where proxies for agency costs are higher.
frase_slide: VCs choose round timing by weighing agency and monitoring costs (Gompers, 1995)
dati_metodo: Random sample of 794 US venture capital-backed firms, 1961-1992 (Venture Economics); Weibull duration regressions, Poisson regressions for number of rounds, agency-cost theory predictions.

tesi: regression-discontinuity evidence on angel-group funding (a model of point 3).
estrazione: The paper's third set of findings uses a regression discontinuity design on ventures just above and below the funding threshold of two US angel groups, to remove the endogeneity of funding. It finds more survival and better operations above the threshold, qualitative but non-significant support for exit, and no difference in follow-on financing.
citazione: Our third set of findings considers ventures just above and below the funding threshold by using the regression discontinuity methodology
frase_paper: Kerr et al. (2014) use a regression discontinuity around the funding threshold of two US angel groups to study the outcomes of funded versus rejected ventures.
frase_slide: Regression discontinuity around angel funding threshold gives quasi-experimental evidence on funding (Kerr et al., 2014)
dati_metodo: Confidential deal records of two US angel groups (Tech Coast Angels, CommonAngels), ventures pitched 2001-2006, outcomes to Dec 2010; OLS comparisons plus a fuzzy regression discontinuity around the angels' interest threshold (130 deals).
numero_chiave: About a 32 percentage point jump in the probability of angel funding above the border (Table 5, 0.316-0.328, N = 130)
limiti_vs_noi: Two large, professionally managed US angel groups (Tech Coast Angels, CommonAngels), 130 deals pitched 2001-2006, outcomes to Dec 2010; angels, not VC; the authors say effects are likely at the upper end of the angel population. Not a VC setting and not a gap or hype design.
note: The parenthetical 'a model of point 3' is about the repo's own design, not something the txt can confirm; only the RD evidence on angel funding is judged. The design is fuzzy.

tesi: VC follows the economy down (supply-side variation).
estrazione: The paper shows that VC deal activity is strongly pro-cyclical: it falls in recessions, especially early-stage. On whether the cause is supply, it is more cautious: all forces (investment opportunities, entrepreneurs' human capital, supply frictions) are likely at play, and the early-stage concentration and the fundraising-timing test are said to suggest or support a capital-supply friction. In the COVID-19 episode the authors argue supply was not constrained.
citazione: All of these forces are likely at play, to a greater or lesser extent, in recessions.
frase_paper: Howell et al. (2020) show that VC deal activity falls in recessions, especially at the early stage, and argue that frictions in the supply of capital are a likely, though not the only, mechanism.
frase_slide: VC activity falls in recessions; supply frictions are a likely, not sole, channel (Howell et al., 2020)
dati_metodo: US VC deals 1976-2017 (Refinitiv VentureXpert) matched to all US patents; panel regressions of deal volume and patent quality on NBER recession months; plus COVID-19 early look with PitchBook and CB Insights deal counts (March-April 2020)
numero_chiave: Early-stage VC deals down about 38% in the two months from 4 March 2020 vs the previous four months
limiti_vs_noi: Recession and COVID-19 shocks, not within-sector hype variation in a boom period; patent-quality tests, no startup exit outcomes.
note: Compound tesi: 'follows the economy down' is shown; 'supply-side variation' is only suggestive and one of several mechanisms, which decided the esito.
